content:
Users can now create fully licensed music tracks, voiceovers and sound effects on Adobe's Firefly AI assistant. Here are the details.

Firefly audio tools now officially launched

Adobe previously partnered with Berklee College of Music to conduct a survey aimed at understanding the workflows and challenges faced by video creators, musicians and marketers. Adobe said 100% of respondents said their videos use music, with 32.7% using AI-generated music. 43.2% said legal and copyright risks were the main obstacle to their use of music, while 38.9% blamed licensing fees.

Adobe today officially launched the Generate Music tool on Firefly, along with two other tools: Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects:

Generate Music can create original, fully licensed music tracks that can also be tailored to the length and mood of your video, so your music can be used on any platform without worrying about licensing or takedown issues. Generate Speech can transform scripts into clear, natural-sounding voiceovers. You can choose to use Adobe's own Firefly voice model or ElevenLabs. Generate Sound Effects can create custom sound effects that match the action, rhythm and energy of your content.

The company stressed that what Generate Music creates is fully licensed, production-ready music, and like Generate Speech and Generate Sound Effects, it requires no additional subscription to generate commercially safe assets.

Generate Music can analyse video content and create editable prompts based on the most suitable soundtrack it identifies. Users can also adjust parameters such as the music's tempo, energy and length before pressing "Generate", with four options available each time.

When using Generate Speech, users can add emotional expression and pronunciation tags to specific parts of the script; while Generate Sound Effects lets users type a text prompt, or record a sound effect with their own voice, as a reference for generating the audio.

Below is Adobe's response:

The new tools are now available on Adobe Firefly's desktop and mobile web apps.

Adobe expands AI model lineup within Firefly

In addition, Adobe announced today that Gemini Omni Flash has joined Firefly, allowing users to "input prompts with text alongside video, audio and images, giving you more ways to create video, reshaping it through repeated revisions, [...]."

This move comes just days after Adobe added Runway Aleph 2.0 and Kling 2.0 to its third-party model toolkit, which already had models from Google, Kling AI, Luma AI, OpenAI, Runway and Adobe itself.
